$comment: Variant module: STRATEGY_MEMO. Byline: Claude Code · Opus 5 · 2026-08-29 13:00 EDT. Parent registry: ../document-markdown-v1.json. Emits no artifact — chunk pass only.

detect.resolution_note: Deliberately LAST in the registry resolution_order — its detect rules are the loosest, so more specific variants must be tried first.

pass_chunk.strategy: one chunk per heading section; single whole-file chunk if the document is under chunk_size
pass_chunk.rationale: Short and self-contained. Over-chunking destroys the argument structure — each section is one framing move and only makes sense whole.
pass_chunk.structure_note: The reference instance places blockquoted proposed courtroom phrasing under each numbered heading. A blockquote and its heading belong in the same chunk.

artifact_rationale: Owner work product — strategy and framing, not fact. Nothing here is an event that belongs on a timeline, and treating argumentation as fact would be a category error with evidentiary consequences.

known_content_hazards.escaped_ordinals: Headings contain escaped ordinals (e.g. an escaped '1.'). Treat the backslash as source text, not markup.
known_content_hazards.proposed_speech: Blockquoted content is PROPOSED phrasing — language the owner might use — not something said, filed, or on the record. It must never be extracted as an assertion of fact or as a quotation from the record. This is the single most important hazard in this variant.

open_questions: Whether strategy memos should carry a distinguishing marker so retrieval can separate owner argumentation from source material. Relates to EvidenceCitation.epistemic_class on the Legal-Workspace side, which already distinguishes legal_theory from established_fact.
